findings.highlight: If that happensit’ll just be more painful
findings.evidenceJa: そうなった時無抵抗なまま殺されるのは
findings.governingReading: If that happens, being killed without resistance would impose the greater pain on Rin.
findings.explanation: Missing separation fuses “happens” and “it’ll” at the causal turn of Shirou’s reasoning.

findings.highlight: it’ll just be more painful for Tohsaka if I get killed by her without putting up a fight
findings.evidenceJa: なにより遠坂に辛い思いを押し付ける事になる
findings.governingReading: Above all, allowing himself to be killed without resistance would amount to forcing a painful burden upon Rin.
findings.explanation: The English preserves Rin’s pain but removes 押し付ける, the core of Shirou’s reasoning that his passivity would actively impose that suffering on her.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂とは敵同士に戻る。
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Rin will return to being enemies of one another.
findings.explanation: This branch again turns the reciprocal 敵同士 relation into Rin alone becoming Shirou’s enemy.

findings.highlight: That’s what you want, right, Saber?
findings.evidenceJa: それでいいんだろ、セイバー
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks Saber whether that understanding of the terms is correct or acceptable.
findings.explanation: “What you want” assigns Saber a personal desire for renewed enmity, replacing Shirou’s request to confirm the conclusion she pressed him to recognize.

findings.highlight: When that time comeswill I be able to fight Tohsaka like Saber said?
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はその時セイバーに告げた通り、遠坂と戦う事が出来るのだろうか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether, when the time comes, he can fight Rin as he himself just told Saber he would.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the speech relation and attributes the operative statement to Saber, erasing that Shirou is testing his future conduct against his own declared commitment.

findings.highlight: When that time comeswill I be able to fight Tohsaka
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はその時セイバーに告げた通り
findings.governingReading: When that time comes, Shirou asks whether he can act as stated.
findings.explanation: Missing separation fuses “comes” and “will” at the beginning of the scene’s closing self-question.

findings.highlight: I do not have anything to say if you understand. We shall cooperate with Rin and have you experience more battles.
findings.evidenceJa: それを理解してくれているのなら、私からは何もありません。凛と協力し、シロウの戦闘経験を増やすとしましょう
findings.governingReading: If Shirou understands that condition, Saber has no further objection; they will cooperate with Rin to increase his combat experience.
findings.explanation: The first sentence sounds like inability or refusal to speak rather than absence of objection, while “have you experience more battles” awkwardly substitutes battle count for accumulated combat experience.

findings.highlight: We will eventually fight as long as we’re alive.
findings.evidenceJa: 生き延びている限り、いずれ対決の時が来る。
findings.governingReading: So long as Shirou survives, the time for an eventual confrontation will come.
findings.explanation: The English invents a plural “we” and turns the arrival of a future confrontation into a categorical joint action, obscuring Shirou’s survival-conditioned fatalism.
